name: Cai ASB
question: Does treating asymptomatic bacteriuria prevent symptomatic recurrence in young women with recurrent urinary tract infection?

arms.label: No antibiotic treatment for asymptomatic bacteriuria
antibiotic treatment guided by urine-culture susceptibility

design.population: Sexually active women aged 18–40 years with recurrent symptomatic urinary tract infection and asymptomatic bacteriuria confirmed by the same uropathogen at at least 10^5 CFU/mL on two consecutive urine cultures.
design.locator: Full text, Study Schedule, p 772; Figure 1, p 773; Results, p 774

verdictNote: At 12 months, more women remained recurrence-free without treatment; reported recurrence RRs differ from crude ratios.
takeaway: In young women with recurrent urinary tract infection and asymptomatic bacteriuria, withholding antibiotics yielded more women recurrence-free through 12 months than susceptibility-guided treatment (237/312 [76.0%] versus 62/361 [17.2%] among analyzed women; Kaplan–Meier P = 0.003).

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Cai T, Mazzoli S, Mondaini N, et al. "The Role of Asymptomatic Bacteriuria in Young Women With Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections: To Treat or Not to Treat?" *Clin Infect Dis.* 2012;55(6):771-777. doi:10.1093/cid/cis534
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results, p 774; Table 2, p 775

results.measure: Women remaining asymptomatic after the three scheduled visits among the original analyzed groups
results.note: Counts are derived from the final asymptomatic row of Table 2 over the initially analyzed groups. The reported Kaplan–Meier comparison of recurrence had RR 2.14 (SE 0.187; P = 0.003), without a confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Study Schedule, p 773; Table 2 and Kaplan–Meier Results, p 775

results.measure: Symptomatic women among those remaining after symptomatic women at the 3-month visit were censored
results.note: The reported RR does not equal the crude ratio of these visit-specific risks; percentages are recalculated from Table 2 counts.
results.locator: Full text, Follow-up Results, p 774; Table 2, p 775

results.measure: New symptomatic episodes among women remaining after symptomatic women at the 3- and 6-month visits were censored
results.note: The abstract instead divides these episode counts by initial analyzed groups (41/312 [13.1%] and 169/361 [46.8%]); the reported RR does not equal either crude risk ratio.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 771; Follow-up Results and Table 2, p 775

results.endpoint: Quality of Well-Being score at 12 months
results.measure: Mean score at the final scheduled visit; higher scores indicate better quality of life
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Follow-up Results, p 775

harms.label: Pyelonephritis during 12-month follow-up
harms.note: The article reports no significant between-group difference.

harms.label: Antimicrobial adverse events
harms.note: No denominator for women receiving antimicrobial therapy is supplied.

delivery.label: Bacteriuria and symptomatic UTI management
delivery.value: No antibiotic was given for asymptomatic bacteriuria in group A; group B received antibiotic therapy selected by antibiogram. Symptomatic UTIs in either group were cultured and treated by susceptibility.

delivery.label: Antibiotics used for asymptomatic bacteriuria
delivery.value: In the treated group, fosfomycin trometamol 31.4%, nitrofurantoin 26.8%, co-trimoxazole 19.8%, ciprofloxacin 13.1%, and levofloxacin 8.9% were used.
delivery.note: The paper reports percentages without drug-specific counts.

delivery.label: Scheduled surveillance
delivery.value: Follow-up visits and urine cultures were scheduled at 3, 6, and 12 months regardless of symptoms; symptomatic women between visits were asked to contact the center and undergo microbiological testing.

reports.label: Long-term observational follow-up
reports.citation: Cai T, Nesi G, Mazzoli S, et al. "Asymptomatic Bacteriuria Treatment Is Associated With a Higher Prevalence of Antibiotic Resistant Strains in Women With Urinary Tract Infections." *Clin Infect Dis.* 2015;61(11):1655-1661. doi:10.1093/cid/civ696
reports.followUp: Mean 38.8 months; 550/673 women from the initial analyzed cohort completed follow-up
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Abstract, p 1655; Study Population, p 1656; Figure 2, p 1659

results.note: Complete-case observational follow-up of the original randomized groups.
results.locator: Full text, Clinical Findings, p 1657; Table 2, p 1660

results.measure: Resistant isolates among E. coli from symptomatic UTIs
results.note: Isolate-level comparison among women with symptomatic recurrence; the paper names antibiotic resistance as the main outcome.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1656; Table 2, p 1660

results.measure: Resistant isolates among E. coli from symptomatic UTIs
results.note: Isolate-level comparison among women with symptomatic recurrence; the paper names antibiotic resistance as the main outcome.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1656; Table 2, p 1660

results.measure: Resistant isolates among E. coli from symptomatic UTIs
results.note: Isolate-level comparison among women with symptomatic recurrence; the paper names antibiotic resistance as the main outcome. Other tested drugs showed no significant difference; susceptibility differences first appeared at 2-year follow-up.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1656; Table 2, p 1660

results.endpoint: Quality of Well-Being score at long-term follow-up
results.measure: Mean score among 550 women retained for analysis; higher scores indicate better quality of life
results.locator: Full text, Questionnaires and Clinical Findings, p 1657; Table 2, p 1660

harms.label: Pyelonephritis during long-term follow-up
harms.locator: Full text, Clinical Findings, p 1657; Table 2, p 1660

harms.label: Antimicrobial adverse effects among women treated for symptomatic UTI
harms.note: All 301 symptomatic women received antibiotics; adverse effects were recorded but not included in the analysis.

delivery.label: Follow-up surveillance
delivery.value: Visits were scheduled every 6 months or more often for symptoms. No microbiological evaluation was scheduled for asymptomatic women. Symptomatic episodes were cultured and treated by susceptibility; treated women remained in follow-up, and isolates from multiple episodes were collected.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Schedule and Data Collection, p 1656

delivery.label: Antibiotics for symptomatic episodes
delivery.value: Among 301 symptomatic women, 85 received fosfomycin trometamol, 59 nitrofurantoin, 37 amoxicillin–clavulanic acid, 35 co-trimoxazole, and 30 ciprofloxacin; other antibiotics accounted for the remainder.
